query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is the direct target metric of the query (resolution time), computed as a duration derivable from opened_at and closed_at timestamps present in the table. It gives the core continuous axis needed to compare across category, priority, and assignment group. Samples show only closed_at/sys_updated_on, but opened_at exists in the table, so the derivation is warranted; values look plausible. NULLs for unresolved rows are correct behaviour.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: The table already contains an original 'priority' column, and this appears to be a near-restatement of it as a numeric level. It offers little new analytical leverage since priority is a query dimension already available. Values are grounded in the existing priority field. Slightly useful if it normalizes/cleans priority, but largely redundant.

per_column.name: priority_category
per_column.rationale: A textual labeling (Critical/High/Moderate) of the same priority information, redundant with both the original 'priority' column and the added priority_level. It provides marginally more interpretability for grouping but is essentially a restatement. The mapping (2->High, 1->Critical, 3->Moderate) is a sound categorization of priority values, though the label assignment is a convention rather than stated in text.

judge.rationale: The augmentation delivers the single most important column for this query, resolution_time_hours, which is both highly useful and soundly grounded in the table's timestamp fields. The remaining two columns (priority_level, priority_category) are largely redundant restatements of the existing 'priority' column and of each other, adding limited analytical leverage. Groundedness is generally strong across all columns with no hallucinations observed; produced values are sound readings of the source timestamps and priority field.
